review_cost.rationale: Approve after one light round of nits — no blocking defects, no rework; the asks are consolidation (shared types/utils) and small clarity fixes.

findings.issue: Server routes return untyped any shapes while each page hand-declares a matching interface (app/app/pages/types/[name].vue:6, app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:9); the API contract can drift silently between the two halves of the app.
findings.suggestion: Declare the response types once in shared/types/ (auto-imported in both app/ and server/ in Nuxt 4) and annotate the defineEventHandler returns with them.

findings.issue: humanize is duplicated verbatim in app/app/utils/format.ts:3 and app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:51.
findings.suggestion: Move it (and orDash/queryString if useful server-side) to shared/utils/ so both bundles use one implementation.

findings.issue: Game labels are built by correlating gameRecords with [...gameNames][i] across two independent Set spreads; correct but fragile under refactoring.
findings.suggestion: Create const gameNamesArr = [...gameNames] once and zip records with it, or map over the Set entries directly.

findings.issue: page is clamped to totalPages for display, but an out-of-range ?page= stays in the URL.
findings.suggestion: Either replace the URL with the clamped page or leave the raw page in the URL and let the visible slice follow it; pick one source of truth.

findings.issue: scrollBehaviorType: 'auto' is the framework default; the line is configuration noise.
findings.suggestion: Delete the router.options block (or set it only if 'smooth' hash scrolling is wanted).

findings.issue: hidden is smuggled into the pokemon ref via object spread and then extracted by the extra callback — indirect and hard to read.
findings.suggestion: Have cardsFor accept a per-ref record (e.g. Map<id, boolean>) or pass {ref, hidden} pairs explicitly.

findings.issue: vue and vue-router are listed as direct dependencies; Nuxt resolves and manages these versions itself.
findings.suggestion: Drop them and let Nuxt's dependency graph provide them, avoiding version drift.

findings.issue: The 5000-entry cache cap only evicts expired entries on insert, so the bound is soft and eviction is O(n) inline.
findings.suggestion: Fine at this data volume; if kept, note it's a soft cap or evict oldest entries regardless of expiry.

findings.issue: First request to a Pokémon page issues one upstream fetch per learned move (hundreds for Move-tutors), all in parallel.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given the 60s cache and local API; if it ever matters, batch or lazily fetch move details per selected game.

findings.issue: TypeRef is re-declared identically in types/[name].vue and pokemon/[name].vue, and similar near-duplicate row interfaces exist per page.
findings.suggestion: Hoist shared shape types to shared/types/ and reuse them across pages and the corresponding server routes.

summary: A well-built Nuxt 4 app that uses the framework's current primitives almost everywhere and keeps a crisp server-routes/ thin-pages boundary. The main review asks are consolidation — shared types and utils instead of duplicated helpers and hand-mirrored interfaces — plus a few clarity and config nits. No correctness bug of consequence found; I'd approve after one light round.
